artifact: PRHAAR C5 Open Images rotation + integrity probe

q3_decisive_aspect_statistics.method: normalized-aspect statistics on validation Person/Car boxes (depiction/group_of excluded)
q3_decisive_aspect_statistics.reading: Person 90/270 groups flip to ~80-86% wide vs 10.1% wide in the rot=0 control; Car 270 flips to tall vs the wide control; 180 (aspect-preserving) stays tall like the control. Boxes are in the RAW stored-image frame.

interpretation: Q1: downloaded bytes are NOT the original Flickr files -- by design. OI redistributes images resized to max 1024px; the info CSV's OriginalMD5 (base64, not hex) and OriginalSize refer to the ORIGINAL Flickr upload, so 100/100 'mismatches' are expected and are not an integrity problem. Our own integrity anchor is the SHA-256 recorded per image in acquisition_manifest.jsonl.

Q2/Q3: OI bounding boxes are expressed in the coordinate frame of the RAW STORED image (the exact bytes we download) -- NOT the rotated display frame. Evidence: on 90/270-rotation images, Person boxes are 80.0-86.2% WIDE (lying) vs 10.1% wide on rot=0 controls (n=104); Car flips to tall vs its wide control; the aspect-preserving 180 group matches the control. The montages confirm visually: raw panel contains the sideways scene and the box hugs the sideways person.

CONSEQUENCE for PRHAAR C5: no rotation handling is needed anywhere -- raw bytes + raw normalized boxes are frame-consistent. The Rotation field is display metadata only and is recorded per image in the acquisition manifest for QA slicing. Rotation-unknown images (blank, ~13%) are unaffected: annotation correctness never depended on rotation.
